author: Advanced Telerobotics Research Lab
subject: Sponsor and industry partner introduction

slides.title: Partner with Kent State's ATR Lab
slides.subtitle: Telepresence robotics and Physical AI research
notes: Introduce the lab by its full name first: the Advanced Telerobotics Research Lab at Kent State University, in the Department of Computer Science.
For a specific meeting, put the partner's name and the date in the eyebrow (AP style: SEPT. 23, 2026) and open with the partnership idea in their words.
Before the meeting: clear the company with Philanthropy and Alumni Engagement (gifts) or the Office of Sponsored Programs (research agreements).

slides.title: Agenda
panel: Exploring the frontiers of telepresence robotics, tele-embodiment, autonomy and artificial intelligence.
slides.notes: Five parts, about 15 minutes, then questions. The panel quotes the lab's own homepage line.

slides.title: From telepresence to Physical AI
body: Heritage: telepresence, tele-embodiment and immersive teleoperation
Direction: Physical AI that works alongside people
AI that senses and acts in the real world through a robot
Real hardware, from humanoids to quadrupeds
slides.image_alt: Illustration: a remote operator wearing a VR headset controls a distant robot arm over a network link.
notes: The lab opened in 2017 in the Department of Computer Science. Its first decade is telepresence: operating a robot from somewhere else and feeling present in it (the TeleBot line, the AARON AR system for NASA SUITS).
New work leads with Physical AI: robots that sense, decide and act in real settings alongside people. Keep telepresence in the story; it explains the name.
The drawing is a concept illustration, not lab hardware.

slides.title: Three research threads
slides.text1: Robots people operate and inhabit at a distance
slides.text2: Robots that sense, decide and act beside people
slides.text3: Students do real research on real hardware
slides.notes: These are the lab's message pillars 1 to 3. The icons repeat the headings, so they are marked decorative.

slides.title: Platforms and projects today
right_body: PepperKit: Pepper with an LLM voice agent
Expressive Motion on the Booster K1
slides.notes: VendoBot was published in the HRI 2026 Companion proceedings (Edinburgh, March 2026). PepperKit gives Pepper a realtime LLM voice agent. TeleBot-4R has an XR interface for Meta Quest.

slides.title: Recognition and open work
slides.text1: teams selected for the onsite challenge
slides.text2: World Robot Summit Plant Disaster Prevention Challenge
notes: Say it as the proof bank words it: selected as one of the top 10 teams for the onsite NASA SUITS challenge (2020); selected as one of 11 finalists in the World Robot Summit Plant Disaster Prevention Challenge (2021). The Kent Stater reported the lab's team was the only one from the United States; attribute it if you say it.
53 public repositories was the count on Sept. 28, 2026. Recount at github.com/ATR-Lab before presenting.

slides.title: Milestones since 2017
slides.notes: Past projects are labeled with their years. 2020: AARON received the Best Conference Paper Award at IHCI 2020. 2023: the lab's ATR_FLUX team built the second generation of AARON, an AR system for spacesuit operations, for NASA SUITS.

slides.statement: “Creating a cooperative world where robots help humans rather than replace them.”
slides.notes: A pause before the students section. The quotation is the lab's own 2021 wording; keep it word for word.

slides.title: Students and programs
slides.subhead: From high school to doctoral study
body: Summer research internship for high school students
Summer workshop for middle school students
slides.figure_alt: Illustration: three students build a small wheeled robot together at a table.
slides.caption: FIG. 01 // Concept illustration, not a lab photo
slides.notes: The 2026 summer programs are titled Hands-on Physical AI and Robotics, for high school students (internship) and for middle school students (workshop). New Physical AI Agent courses will be offered in 2027. Use real, consented photos when the lab has them.

slides.subtitle: Every route runs through a Kent State office
slides.notes: The ask. Each route below has a university office that handles it; the lab does not negotiate terms itself.

slides.title: How to work with the lab
notes: Sponsored Programs negotiates and accepts research agreements (projects, testing, data, IP). Gifts of money, equipment or camp scholarships go through the Division of Philanthropy and Alumni Engagement (gifts@kent.edu).
Never promise IP terms, exclusivity, deliverables, naming rights or tax treatment: those belong to those offices.

slides.title: Thank you
slides.message: Book a lab visit to see the robots at work.
slides.notes: Visits are by appointment. Follow up within 24 hours with the one-pager and a proposed visit date.
